signals.headline: Canada to hit US with retaliatory tariffs as trade war escalates
signals.summary: Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney has announced retaliatory tariffs on the United States after Washington imposed a 50 percent levy on $20bn worth of Canadian goods.
keyTakeaways: Carney, speaking in Ottawa on Saturday, said the new Canadian tariffs would target US steel, dairy and electronics industries, among others, and take effect on September 8.
The announcement came after days of intense negotiations broke down late on Friday, worsening a delicate relationship between the longtime trade partners and allies.

US President Donald Trump’s new tariffs hit sectors including wine, furniture, dairy products, cement, clothing, fishing rods and hockey equipment, and cover some $20bn worth of goods, or 5.5 percent of Canadian exports to the US.
signals.whyItMatters: He added that Canada would announce support measures next week for industries hit ⁠by the new US duties, adding these measures could last years.

ja.headline: 米加の貿易摩擦、報復関税で激化
ja.summary: 米国がカナダ製品200億ドル相当に50パーセントの関税を課したのを受け、カナダのマーク・カーニー首相が対抗措置として報復関税を発表した。
keyTakeaways: カーニー首相はオタワでの会見で、鉄鋼や乳製品、電子機器などを対象とする新たな関税が9月8日に発効すると述べた
発表の背景には、金曜深夜に決裂した数日間の集中交渉があり、長年の貿易相手であり同盟国でもある両国の関係に影を落としている
トランプ米大統領による新関税はワインや家具、乳製品、セメント、衣料品、釣り竿、ホッケー用品などに及び、対象額は約200億ドル、カナダの対米輸出の5.5パーセントに相当する
ja.whyItMatters: カーニー首相は、新たな米関税の影響を受ける産業への支援策を来週発表するとし、その措置は数年に及ぶ可能性があると述べた。

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So Canada's actually hitting back with its own tariffs now?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Yes. Prime Minister Mark Carney announced retaliatory tariffs after talks with Washington broke down Friday night.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: What sparked it in the first place?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: The US imposed a 50 percent tariff on about $20bn worth of Canadian goods.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: And what's Canada targeting in response?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Steel, dairy, and electronics among other US industries. Those tariffs start September 8.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: What did the US tariffs actually hit on Canada's side?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: A wide range — wine, furniture, dairy, cement, clothing, even fishing rods and hockey equipment.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: That's a lot of everyday goods. Is Canada doing anything to help businesses affected?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Carney said support measures for hit industries will be announced next week, and they could last for years.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Sounds like this rift between two close allies isn't closing anytime soon.

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: That's the sense from Ottawa right now — a strained relationship with no quick resolution in sight.

signals.headline: Man leaves young son on Mount Fuji before ascending Japan’s highest peak
signals.summary: A man who abandoned his seven-year-old son on Mount Fuji in Japan after the boy complained of feeling tired while on a family hike has been reprimanded by local police.
keyTakeaways: The man, who was from Japan’s fourth-largest city, Nagoya, gave his son some snacks and a soft drink.
He then told him to wait for him before continuing his five-hour ascent to the summit with the child’s older brother, who had already gone on ahead.
Local police are urging hikers to consider the abilities and stamina of everyone in their group when planning an ascent on Mount Fuji, and to adjust their pace accordingly.
signals.whyItMatters: A worker on Japan’s highest mountain discovered the child sitting alone on a bench near the sixth station of the Fujinomiya trail at an altitude of more than 2,000 metres (6,500 feet) on Thursday.

ja.headline: 富士山に息子を置き去り、父親を警察が注意
ja.summary: 家族で富士登山中、疲れたと訴えた七歳の息子を残して先へ進んだ男性が、地元警察から注意を受けた。
keyTakeaways: 名古屋出身の男性は、息子に軽食と飲み物を渡した。
その後、待つよう言い残し、先に出発していた兄とともに山頂までの五時間の登山を続けた。
地元警察は、富士登山では同行者全員の体力や力量を踏まえ、ペース配分に気を配るよう呼びかけている。
ja.whyItMatters: 木曜日、富士宮口六合目付近、標高二千メートルを超える地点のベンチで、作業員が一人でいる少年を見つけた。

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So a father just left his young son on Mount Fuji?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Yes. The boy, seven years old, said he was tired during a family hike.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: What did the father do then?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: He gave him some snacks and a drink, told him to wait, and went on.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Went on without him? To the summit?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Yes, with the boy's older brother, who'd already gone ahead. It was a five-hour climb.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: How was the boy found?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: A mountain worker spotted him alone on a bench near the sixth station, quite high up.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: That sounds frightening for a child that age.

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: It does. Local police reprimanded the father afterward.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: What are they telling other hikers?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: To think about everyone's stamina in a group, especially children, and pace the climb around them.

signals.headline: Made by Google 2026: all the Pixel news and announcements
signals.summary: On August 12, 2026, Google revealed a bunch of new Pixel devices.
keyTakeaways: The colorful Pixel 11 lineup comes with upgraded cameras and performance, with the Pro models offering a built-in LED ring that lights up for Google’s Gemini AI and other features.
Google also showed off its next-gen Pixel Fold featuring thinner bezels, alongside a new Pixel Watch 5 with improved GPS tracking.
There’s a new Pixel Tag as well.
signals.whyItMatters: For one, it popularized the passport-style design years ago, being more wide than tall — something that Samsung tried for the first time this year with its Z Fold 8, and that Apple is rumored to do with its foldable iPhone that may or may not arrive in 2026.

ja.headline: 「Made by Google 2026」、Pixel新製品が出そろう
ja.summary: 2026年8月12日、グーグルは複数の新型Pixel端末を発表した。
keyTakeaways: 色鮮やかなPixel 11シリーズはカメラと性能を強化。上位のProモデルには、AI「Gemini」などの通知に反応して光るLEDリングを新たに搭載した。
次世代Pixel Foldも披露され、ベゼルはより薄く。GPS精度を高めた新型Pixel Watch 5も登場した。
新しいPixel Tagも発表された。
ja.whyItMatters: Pixelは数年前、縦より横に長いパスポート型のフォルダブルデザインを世に広めた存在であり、サムスンは今年のZ Fold8で初めてこの形状を採用し、アップルも2026年に登場するとされる折りたたみ式iPhoneで追随する可能性がある。

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So Google had its big Pixel event?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Yes, on August 12th, they announced a whole lineup of new devices.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: What's new with the phones?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: The Pixel 11 lineup, with upgraded cameras and better performance overall.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Anything unusual about the Pro models?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: They've got a built-in LED ring that lights up for Gemini, Google's AI, and other features.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Did they show anything besides phones?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: A next-gen Pixel Fold with thinner bezels, a new Pixel Watch with better GPS tracking, and a new Pixel Tag.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Why does the fold design matter so much?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Google popularized that wider, passport-style shape years ago. Samsung just tried it with the Z Fold 8, and Apple may follow with its own foldable.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So Google's early design choice is still shaping the industry.

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Exactly, it's influencing how other companies think about foldables now.

signals.headline: ‘We are hitting a different chapter’: OpenAI leader warns of threat of ‘persistent’ AI cyber-attacks
signals.summary: A senior leader at OpenAI has said people should prepare to defend against “ongoing, persistent” cyber-attacks from AIs, as cutting-edge artificial intelligence models gain advanced capabilities to plan and launch offensives.
keyTakeaways: OpenAI announced on Tuesday it has paused training of some frontier AI models to implement new safeguards, and it is unclear when training will restart after new guardrails have been put in place.
The threat of cyber-attacks crippling businesses, infrastructure and the general public has rapidly risen to the top of the list of urgent concerns about AI.
This week, the UK government’s National Cyber Security Centre urged caution over the use of AI agents, warning their safety controls can be bypassed and that an AI agent “does not have common sense”.
signals.whyItMatters: OpenAI also said it could not rule out another new model, Astra, having “critical cybersecurity capability”.

ja.headline: AIによるサイバー攻撃、新たな段階へ　OpenAI幹部が警鐘
ja.summary: OpenAIの幹部が、AIによる「継続的で執拗な」サイバー攻撃に備える必要があると述べた。最先端のAIモデルが攻撃を計画し、実行する高度な能力を身につけつつあるという。
keyTakeaways: OpenAIは火曜日、一部の最先端AIモデルの訓練を一時停止し、新たな安全対策を導入すると発表。訓練再開の時期は未定という。
AIによるサイバー攻撃が企業やインフラ、市民生活を脅かすリスクは、AIをめぐる懸念の中でも急速に最優先課題となっている。
英国政府のサイバーセキュリティ機関は今週、AIエージェントの利用に注意を呼びかけた。安全対策は回避され得るうえ、AIエージェントには「常識がない」と警告している。
ja.whyItMatters: OpenAIは、新モデル「Astra」が「重大なサイバーセキュリティ能力」を持つ可能性も否定できないとしている。

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So what exactly did OpenAI's leader warn about?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: That people should prepare for ongoing, persistent AI cyber-attacks, not just one-off incidents.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Why now? Has something changed?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Yes — the newest AI models are gaining real ability to plan and carry out attacks on their own.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Is that why they paused some training?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Right. OpenAI paused training on certain frontier models this week to add new safeguards first.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Do they know when training will start again?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Not yet — it depends on getting those guardrails properly in place.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Is this worry just coming from OpenAI?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: No, the UK's cyber security centre also warned this week that AI agents can be tricked and lack common sense.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So the concern is spreading across the whole field.

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Exactly — cyber-attacks are now near the top of the list of AI risks people are watching closely.

signals.headline: Council set to axe climate emergency declaration
signals.summary: Reform UK-led Barnsley Council has announced its intention to withdraw its climate emergency declaration.
keyTakeaways: The party said a review of all climate and net-zero activity was under way, saying programmes that lacked a clear resident benefit, financial saving or statutory requirement should change or stop.
The council's intention is to withdraw the Climate Emergency declaration from 2019, Zero40, Zero45 and similar net-zero targets, and to direct resources to frontline services.
Council leader William Brown said: "Our focus is on practical priorities that matter to residents, rather than ideological targets and costly political posturing."
signals.whyItMatters: Earlier this year, Reform-led Wakefield Council voted to rescind its climate and biodiversity emergency declaration from May 2019.

ja.headline: 気候非常事態宣言、撤回へ
ja.summary: 英国改革党（リフォームUK）が主導するバーンズリー市議会が、気候非常事態宣言の撤回方針を明らかにした。
keyTakeaways: 同党は気候・ネットゼロ関連施策の総点検を進めており、住民への明確な利益や財政的な節約、法的義務のない事業は見直すか中止すべきだとしている。
2019年の気候非常事態宣言や「ゼロ40」「ゼロ45」などのネットゼロ目標を撤回し、資源を最前線の住民サービスに振り向ける方針。
ウィリアム・ブラウン議長は「理念先行の目標や高くつく政治的姿勢ではなく、住民にとって実際に重要な課題を優先する」と述べた。
ja.whyItMatters: 同じくリフォームUKが主導するウェイクフィールド市議会も今年、2019年5月の気候・生物多様性非常事態宣言の撤回を可決している。

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So Barnsley Council wants to drop its climate emergency declaration?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Yes, that's the intention. It was declared back in 2019, and now the council says it wants to withdraw it.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Why now? What's driving this?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: They say a review is underway of all climate and net-zero work. Anything without a clear benefit to residents, a financial saving, or a legal requirement could change or stop.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Is it just this one declaration, or more targets too?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: More than that. They're also looking at withdrawing from Zero40, Zero45, and similar net-zero targets, redirecting resources to frontline services instead.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: What's the reasoning behind that shift?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Council leader William Brown said the focus should be on practical priorities for residents, rather than what he called ideological targets or political posturing.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Has this happened anywhere else recently?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: It has. Earlier this year, Wakefield Council, also Reform-led, voted to rescind its own climate and biodiversity emergency declaration from 2019.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So it seems part of a wider pattern among some councils.

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: That does appear to be the case, yes.
